question_text: You need to give directions to a friend who wants to visit your house. You would:
option_v: Draw a map or give them a visual map layout
option_a: Tell them the directions over a phone call
option_r: Write down step-by-step street instructions
option_k: Drive or walk with them to show them the route

question_text: You want to learn how to assemble a piece of flat-pack furniture. You would:
option_v: Study the assembly diagrams and schematics
option_a: Ask a friend or family member to explain the process
option_r: Read through the step-by-step written text manual
option_k: Jump straight into fitting the parts together by trial and error

question_text: You are planning a vacation for a group of friends. To get feedback on the plan, you would:
option_v: Show them a visual map and photos of the itinerary
option_a: Call them or host a meeting to talk it through
option_r: Send a detailed written email or document summary
option_k: Plan a mini walkthrough or focus on the physical activities scheduled

question_text: You are learning a new software program or digital tool on your computer. You prefer to:
option_v: Follow flowcharts or UI visual walkthroughs
option_a: Ask a tech expert or listen to a step-by-step podcast tutorial
option_r: Read the user documentation or official text manual
option_k: Dive in immediately and figure it out by clicking around

question_text: You are shopping for a new house or apartment. Before visiting, you prefer:
option_v: A floor plan drawing and map of the neighborhood
option_a: A discussion with the real estate agent or owner
option_r: A detailed printed list of features and specifications
option_k: A video walkthrough showing movement through the space

question_text: You have a medical condition (like knee pain) and want to understand it. You'd prefer the doctor:
option_v: Shows you an anatomical diagram or chart of the joint
option_a: Verbally explains what is happening in detail
option_r: Gives you a medical brochure or pamphlet to read
option_k: Uses a 3D physical model to demonstrate the issue

question_text: You want to learn how to play a new board game or card game. You would:
option_v: Look at diagrams of game setup and board layouts
option_a: Have someone explain the rules aloud and answer questions
option_r: Read the instruction booklet from start to finish
option_k: Start playing a practice round immediately to learn by doing

question_text: When choosing a field of study or career path, you prioritize:
option_v: Working with designs, layouts, maps, or charts
option_a: Communicating and exchanging ideas through discussions
option_r: Working with text, reports, and written information
option_k: Applying practical skills in real-world, hands-on scenarios

question_text: You want to improve your photography skills. You would:
option_v: Examine diagrams showing camera mechanics and settings
option_a: Talk with an experienced photographer and ask questions
option_r: Read the camera instructions and written guidebooks
option_k: Take photos, adjust settings, and evaluate real test shots

question_text: A educational website features a tutorial with multiple components. You learn best from:
option_v: Infographics, diagrams, and graphic charts
option_a: Audio narration and spoken explanations
option_r: Written articles and transcript lists
option_k: Interactive demonstrations or step-by-step videos

question_text: You need to prepare a group presentation on a historical event. You would prefer to:
option_v: Design slides heavy on charts, timelines, and visual images
option_a: Lead the verbal delivery and group speech portions
option_r: Write the research paper, script, and hand-out notes
option_k: Create physical props, models, or perform a reenactment

question_text: When receiving feedback on a test or work project, you prefer:
option_v: Visual graphs tracking performance improvements
option_a: A face-to-face conversation talking through the results
option_r: A detailed written report or written feedback comments
option_k: Reviewing concrete examples of what you executed

question_text: You are shopping for financial options or bank products. You decide by:
option_v: Comparing visual graphs showing interest over time
option_a: Discussing choices with a financial consultant
option_r: Reading printed brochures and terms in detail
option_k: Using an interactive calculator to input custom numbers

question_text: You are selecting a instructor, teacher, or conference speaker. You prefer someone who uses:
option_v: Diagrams, flowcharts, and slide visuals
option_a: Group discussions, Q&As, and conversational lectures
option_r: Comprehensive handouts, books, and assigned readings
option_k: Hands-on experiments, practical models, and demonstrations

question_text: You are trying to learn a new workout routine or physical exercise. You prefer to:
option_v: Study posture diagrams and alignment illustrations
option_a: Listen to a trainer explain the movement cues
option_r: Read a bulleted list of physical steps to follow
option_k: Perform the movement slowly while watching a video demonstration

question_text: When browsing the internet to understand a new subject, you gravitate toward:
option_v: Visually compelling layouts, infographics, and mind maps
option_a: Podcasts, radio interviews, and audio clips
option_r: In-depth written articles, e-books, and blogs
option_k: Hands-on simulation tools and practical video tutorials

question_text: You need to remember a set of technical terms or vocabulary. You choose to:
option_v: Use color-coded mind maps or flashcards with visual icons
option_a: Repeat the terms aloud or discuss them with a study buddy
option_r: Write definitions out repeatedly in a study journal
option_k: Associate terms with physical movements or real-world objects

question_text: You are tasked with researching the history of your local city. You would:
option_v: Gather and compare old maps, photos, and historical blueprints
option_a: Record oral history interviews from longtime residents
option_r: Read old newspaper articles and archived town documents
option_k: Visit local historical sites and examine artifacts directly

question_text: You are trouble-shooting a malfunctioning household appliance. You would:
option_v: Look at a visual diagram of the machine’s internal wiring
option_a: Call customer support to talk through the issue with a technician
option_r: Read the troubleshooting section of the printed user guide
option_k: Open the machine up and test the components directly

question_text: When reflecting on your overall learning style, you feel most engaged when:
option_v: Content is represented in spatial, structured, or visual form
option_a: Concepts are debated and talked through aloud
option_r: Concepts are defined clearly using precise text and words
option_k: Knowledge is applied through real-life context and practice
